static_traits.name: Ai Lin
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no previous psychotherapy/counseling history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe personal experience; often uses absolutist expressions (e.g. 'always'), shows mind reading and overgeneralization; attitude rather negative but willing to try and cooperate; speech rate and logical structure not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I always feel I am losing things, and recently even feel I am losing my mind. This makes me feel incapable, and I worry about how others see me. These feelings have existed for years but worsened markedly after moving to Sweden a few months ago; I am triggered almost daily by situations of 'cannot find or forgetting important items', constantly feeling overwhelmed and anxious.
basic_info.core_demands: The sense of incapability and anxiety about losing things markedly affect my daily life and well-being, so I seek counseling to ease these problems.
growth_experiences: During past stressful periods or major life changes, the experience of 'losing things - feeling incapable' repeatedly occurred; at the time it was usually coped with by seeking support from friends and family; has not yet received psychotherapy or formal intervention.

After moving to Sweden a few months ago, environmental change and adaptation stress markedly worsened symptoms; feeling anxious and overwhelmed almost daily when 'unable to find or forgetting important items', with worries that 'others will think me incapable'.

core_beliefs: I cannot control my life (worried about losing my mind)

special_situations.event: After moving to Sweden, often unable to find or forgetting important items, adaptation stress markedly increased
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I keep losing things in the new environment, it shows I cannot manage life; others will also think me incapable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries organizing and mindfulness practice; reduces discussions with family and friends to avoid being looked down on
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am about to lose my mind; others will think me incompetent

special_situations.event: A neighbor glanced over when I could not find the keys once
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others see me flustered, they will definitely think I am very incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hurrying to search harder and using organizing skills, avoiding communicating with others about the current embarrassment and unease
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She must think I am completely incompetent

special_situations.event: Anxiety triggered almost daily when unable to find or forgetting important items
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot manage to never lose anything, it proves I cannot do anything right
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent self-monitoring and sorting, trying to avoid problems through perfect organization
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always lose things; I cannot do anything well

special_situations.event: Choosing not to talk about it when thinking of telling friends or family about the current distress, out of embarrassment and fear of judgment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I expose these feelings and distress, others will think me incapable or will not understand me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids help-seeking and self-disclosure, tries to bear it alone and self-repair with organizing and mindfulness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not understand, cannot help, and will look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen by others as capable, to be understood and accepted, and to keep a sense of control over life
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being judged as incapable, of being rejected, or of losing control over self and life ('losing one's mind')
defense_goal: Maintains stability through organization and self-control; avoids self-disclosure to reduce the risk of being judged

object_relations.self_representation: A clumsy, incapable person who loses things easily and may lose control
object_relations.object_representation: Picky onlookers/judges (others will stare at my mistakes)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor presses 'what evidence is there that the neighbor thinks you incapable' and invites the client to test the mind-reading thought
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting the inner sense of incapability and shame onto others, tending to read others' glances as judgment (transference: projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First acknowledges the lack of solid evidence but insists that 'feelings are facts'; the tone is hesitant, repeatedly emphasizing others' views; when questioned further, turns instead to describing others' expressions and speculations, avoiding going deeper into their own feelings.

manifestations: Having social support yet not confiding the current distress to family and friends out of embarrassment and fear of judgment
Feeling discomfort and increased isolation in the unfamiliar culture and environment
After relocating to a foreign country, her sense of self-control is shaken; worries about 'losing her mind'
Countering uncertainty with high organization and self-monitoring
outcomes: Excessive pursuit of control and tension
Decreased flexibility, increased anxiety and feelings of shame

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Knowing family and friends are supportive yet not seeking help out of embarrassment, turning energy toward self-monitoring and self-blame
Substitutes external support with excessive organizing / mindfulness self-regulation

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Reading the neighbor's glance as judgment of one's 'incapability'
Generally assuming others will look down on one, thus avoiding communication

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-scrutiny and self-blame ('I always lose things')
Excessively worries about others' evaluations in social interaction; very cautious

positive_force: Has relative and friend support resources (historically able to rely on them to cope with difficulties)
Willing to try behavioral experiments and question automatic thoughts under guidance
Proactively tries self-help strategies such as organizing and mindfulness
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as overgeneralization and mind reading lead to persistent self-denial
Environmental and cultural adaptation after moving abroad increased stress and uncertainty
Shame and worry about being judged lead to avoiding help and self-isolation
Catastrophizing and fear of losing control worsen the anxiety experience

target_behavior.behavior: Intense anxiety with self-denial when unable to find or forgetting items ('I cannot do anything well / others will think me incapable')
antecedent: Situations of being unable to find or forgetting important items
After moving to Sweden, faces an unfamiliar environment and adaptation pressure
Others' glances or presence (triggering worries of being judged)
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of being judged as incapable by others and catastrophizing cognitions (worries about losing control / 'losing one's mind'), with a tendency toward external validation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding judgment and uncertainty, gaining a brief sense of control through self-monitoring and organizing behaviors
target_behavior.consequence: Daily life markedly disrupted, productivity and well-being declining, interpersonal relationships affected (less help-seeking and communication)
